itemdesc-saltcrystal-dry: Some things need to be crushed.
item-handbooktext-saltcrystal-dry: This item will only be produced when simmered in a mini cauldron or full-sized cauldron. Saucepans are too small to fit the minimum amount of water required.
item-handbooktext-saltcrystal-damp: These damp salt crystals are produced by sealing brine or salt water into a barrel for 10 days. They will dry out in 14 days, and may be crushed into powder form afterwards.
itemdesc-softresin: Needs 700-1000 mL and 10 days to harden into resin.
item-handbooktext-softresin:
Collected by placing a spile into an acacia or pine log and a liquid container directly beneath it.
Pine trees produce resin from March to November.
Acacia trees produce resin from April to September.
itemdesc-hardresin: Dump out a bucket full of hardened resin to acquire resin.
item-handbooktext-hardresin: Liquid resin that has hardened, but is still inside of a liquid container. While holding the container, press Ctrl+ to empty it onto the ground, producing a chunk of resin.
itemdesc-breadcrumbfeed: Feed comprised of various bread crumbs.
item-handbooktext-breadcrumbfeed: This is an ideal food to make when there are too many types of bread crumbs floating around, although it isn't edible for Seraphs. Many animals will eat it, making it a very cheap food option for maintaining livestock populations.
itemdesc-washedeggshell: Purified by water, ready for pressure.
item-handbooktext-washedeggshell: After being soaked, these egg shells have lost many nutrients. However, this loss has made it easier to grind the shells and utilize the lime left within.
efchefstricksguide-text:
Expanded Foods: Chef's Tricks
Knowledge is power, and power cooks.
REQUIRES 'A CULINARY ARTILLERY' AND 'EXPANDED FOODS: CORE' MODS TO FUNCTION

Introduction
Expanded Foods adds a few items and tools that have non-culinary uses, for the open mind. This guide will help you get more out of your kitchen and make your life a little easier!

Bread Crumb Feed
Breadcrumbs can now be placed into the crafting grid to make bread crumb animal feed, which isn't terribly nutritious but can be rather abundant.

Fun with Oil
Food oil can be produced many ways in Expanded Foods, and has a few critical uses beyond cooking:
- Can be used to make angled gears, clutches, transmissions, windmill rotors, wooden axles, and wooden toggles.
- Can be combined with resin or beeswax and peat to make candles.
Lard can be used in place of oil for any of these recipes.

Resin Production
Fresh Resin can be collected with a spile from pine trees in March through November; or acacia trees in April through September. Give it time to harden and dump it out of its container to get your resin.

Salt Production
Seal 10 L of salt water or 5 L of brine in a barrel to make a damp salt crystal. You can also Boil the same amounts to get a dry salt crystal. You can seal 25 L of water with 1 halite stone in a barrel to output 25 L of salt water, making Halite worth 2.5 salt if you fully optimize the process. Damp salt crystals must dry into dried salt crystals. Dried salt crystals can be ground in the quern to make salt.

Washed Eggshells
Have a bunch of eggshells you don't know what to do with? Animals tired of eating them? Seal 8 eggshells in a barrel with 1 L of water to wash them. 1 washed bundle of eggshells makes 1 handful of lime.
aculinaryartillery:block-handbooktext-sp:
A metal peg that broaches liquid from various trees. Whether or not a tree produces liquid depends on the time of year, as trees produce more or less sap, gum, or nectar during certain seasons. Tapping a tree creates a small wound in the bark that allows sap to flow like blood, albeit slowly.
It can produce birch sap or maple sap, or resin - depending on the tree.
game:item-handbooktext-resin:
Resin is found leaking from the trunks of pine and acacia trees. Pines can be found in all but the most inhospitable and extreme climates, while acacias are found in dry tropical climates only. Resin is also an ingredient for pitch glue.

Liquid resin can be collected from acacia/pine trees using a spile.
Pine trees produce resin from March to November.
Acacia trees produce resin from April to September.
